newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: VENEZUELA JULY CAR SALES UP 145 PCT VS JULY 1996.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELA JULY CAR SALES UP 145 PCT VS JULY 1996.

text.p: Vehicle sales in Venezuela jumped 145.3 percent in July to 14,205 units compared to 5,790 in July 1996, the Venezuelan Automobile Chamber (CAVENEZ) said.
Vehicle sales over the first seven months of the year were up 161.8 percent at 74,736 units compared to 28,546 in the same period of 1996, the CAVENEZ figures showed.
Vehicle sales in July were also up 8.8 percent from 13,058 units in June 1997.
Following a sluggish year in 1996 as Venezuela's economy contracted 1.6 percent, vehicle sales rose sharply to record nine consecutive months of year-on-year rises.
Government officials have pointed to the sharp hike in vehicle sales as an indication that the economy will grow by about four percent this year.
Of the 14,205 units sold domestically in July, 12,177 or 86 percent were assembled in Venezuela and 2,028 or 14 percent were imported.
Of the 74.736 units sold during the first seven months of 1997, 64,056 or 86 percent were assembled in Venezuela and 10,680 or 14 percent were imported.

Vehicle exports in July rose 23.9 percent to 1,978 units from 1,596 in July 1996. Exports over the first seven months of 1997 were up 46.6 percent at 12,085 units, from 8,243 in the same period of 1996.

General Motors Corp led the Venezuelan market with 30 percent of total sales in July. Ford Motor Company followed with 19 percent, Chrysler Corp with 15 percent Toyota Motor Corp with 13 percent, Mitsubishi Motors with 10 percent and Fiat SpA with nine percent with the remainder distributed among several smaller companies.
